description: 2x2 isolation of PM2 strength vs PVS1 gate on the ClinGen eRepo benchmark. All cells use strict point-system combining, full evidence, cohort n=15334, expert P/LP denominator=6476. Only two dials vary: PM2 strength (Moderate vs Supporting) and the PVS1 Very-Strong gate (buggy pLI vs fixed ClinGen-curated LoF mechanism). gnomAD/VEP/REVEL inputs identical (shared SQLite cache).

counterfactual_moderate_fixed_pvs1.label: Counterfactual: v0.18.2 config WITH the PVS1 fix

pvs1_fix_effect_at_moderate.note: Holding PM2 at Moderate, applying the correct PVS1 gate moves sensitivity 69.6% -> 67.1%. The fix is nearly sensitivity-neutral at Moderate: it reclassifies which variants reach Very Strong but does not materially change the P/LP count, because at Moderate most LoF variants already cleared the Likely-Pathogenic threshold through PM2's extra point. PPV rises slightly (0.86 -> 0.878).

pm2_strength_effect_with_fixed_pvs1.note: Holding the PVS1 gate correct, moving PM2 Moderate -> Supporting is the dominant driver: 67.1% -> 47.3%. This is the real, guideline-concordant conservatism of PM2 at Supporting under strict combining.

conclusion: v0.18.2 had no sensitivity-inflating bug. Its 69.6% is a faithful measurement; with the PVS1 fix applied to the same config it would have scored 67.1% (nearly identical). The 69.6% -> 47.3% headline drop is almost entirely the deliberate PM2 Moderate -> Supporting calibration (-19.8pp), not the PVS1 correction (-2.5pp). The PVS1 bug was a correctness defect in the Very-Strong tier distribution, not a sensitivity error; at Moderate it was masked because PM2's point already carried most LoF variants over the LP line.
